question: Does Vallejo and Soriano (2011) report a new Marikina fish occurrence or population count, and can its field sample be linked to the 2010 Jumawan proceedings or the later 2010-2011 five-station life-history sample?

source.title: A matrix population model of the “janitor fish” Pterygoplichthys (Pisces: Loricariidae) in the Marikina River, Luzon island, Philippines and the possibility of controlling this invasive species
source.citation: Vallejo, B. M., Jr., & Soriano, K. A. (2011). A matrix population model of the “janitor fish” Pterygoplichthys (Pisces: Loricariidae) in the Marikina River, Luzon island, Philippines and the possibility of controlling this invasive species. Philippine Science Letters, 4(1), 11–17.
source.accessMethod: Reviewed the journal-hosted full-text PDF, including abstract, introduction, materials and methods, model-input discussion, results, acknowledgements, author contributions, and references. No PDF copy, figure, table, raw measurements, or model workbook was retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The reviewed PDF did not identify an item-specific open license or separate reuse grant. This record summarizes citation and methodological scope only; it does not redistribute article text, tables, figures, data, or images.

studyScope.waterbodyAsReported: Marikina River, as named in the article title and model scope; the article does not resolve the field-sampled reach or station locations.
studyScope.sourceReportedTaxon: Pterygoplichthys Gill, 1858 (genus-level in the article title, abstract, and model).
studyScope.studyType: A stage-based Lefkovitch population model using field and laboratory life-history information and published literature, with a field-collected fish sample reported for fecundity estimation.

fieldSample.sourceStatement: The methods state that 200 fish were collected from the field, measured for size and weight, and dissected for gonad-based fecundity estimation.
fieldSample.stationOrReach: Marikina River is the model locality, but no field station, reach, barangay, or per-site allocation is stated for the 200 fish.
fieldSample.coordinates: None reported for the field sample.
fieldSample.vouchersOrAccessions: None reported in the reviewed paper.

modelInputsAndOutputs.inputLineage: The abstract says matrix elements were derived from field and laboratory life-history work and published literature. The methods specifically say replacement number, estimated annual growth rate, generation time, and average age at spawning were taken from Jumawan et al. (2010). Other stage parameters include assumptions, literature values, and mortality functions.
modelInputsAndOutputs.interpretation: These are outputs of the authors’ specified population model and assumptions, not observed abundance, a census, a catch total, catch-per-unit-effort, or current growth measurement.

studyScope.interpretation: The paper contains a reported field sample, but it is not a dated, gear- and station-resolved fish survey. Preserve the 200-fish count as a study-method detail only; do not create site-level occurrence rows or a present-day population claim from it.

related2010Proceedings.relationship: The 2011 reference list cites this 2010 BAR National Research Symposium contribution (Vol. 1, pp. 1-15), with a distinct title and venue from the separately reviewed NAST BS-39 abstract. The original BAR contribution was not retrieved.
related2010Proceedings.decision: Register the reference separately from NAST. Do not infer that the matrix paper’s 200 fish are the BAR contribution’s sample or that the BAR and NAST items are independent samples.

related2016LifeHistoryStudy.relationship: The 2016 paper reports a July 2010–June 2011 five-station Marikina study and an aggregate 1,133 host-fish sample. The 2011 model article is submitted October 2010 and gives no date or station for its 200 field-collected fish. The topic, river, and overlapping research team/context allow a possible connection, but there are no individual identifiers or sample crosswalk.
related2016LifeHistoryStudy.decision: Do not add 200 to 1,133, treat the 200 as a separate independent survey, or allocate either sample among stations or regions.

related2011BarcodeStudy.relationship: The separate COI article reports genus-level Pterygoplichthys samples from named Marikina-system stations and discusses unresolved P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus boundaries. The matrix paper gives no voucher or accession identifiers tying its 200 field fish to those barcode specimens.
related2011BarcodeStudy.decision: Keep the matrix source label at genus rank and do not use the barcode study to identify the 200 fish.

publicationLineage.independenceDecision: The 2011 paper is a distinct publication containing field/lab and model material, but the 200-fish sample lineage relative to related proceedings and the later five-station study is unresolved. Its model outputs are not an independent population count.

related2010NastAbstract.relationship: The matrix paper cites the BAR proceedings entry, not the separately reviewed NAST citation. The NAST abstract is a related bibliographic item found in the broader Marikina literature; shared authors and topic do not connect its sample to the 200 field fish.
related2010NastAbstract.decision: Keep publication and sample relationships unresolved; do not merge or add counts.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain as historical, research-only Marikina River host-fish/model context. Keep the 200-fish field sample separate from model outputs and unresolved related publication cohorts. Add no species assertion or site-resolved occurrence.

nonClaims: The model estimate lambda = 1.079 and r = 0.076 are not observed abundance, a population census, catch total, catch rate, or current population trend.
The reported 200 fish are a fecundity research sample, not an estimate of Marikina River population size or fishery landings.
The paper does not give the 200 fish collection date, gear, station/reach, site allocation, coordinates, vouchers, or accession identifiers.
The source taxon is genus-level Pterygoplichthys; background mentions of named species do not independently identify the sampled fish.

No sample overlap or independence is established among the 200 fish, the cited 2010 Bureau of Agricultural Research proceedings, the separately reviewed 2010 NAST abstract, the 2011 barcode series, and the 2016 five-station sample.
The paper does not establish present-day occurrence, current abundance, catchability, fishing access, legal catchability, food or water safety, or natural-diet guidance.
No coordinates, geometry, specimen images, or public app content are derived from the paper.
nextActions: Keep this article and its 200 field-sample detail research-only while NCR and CALABARZON freshwater source discovery continues.
Resolve the 2010 Bureau of Agricultural Research proceedings citation and any sample lineage only if a full copy, dated field methods, specimen list, or voucher crosswalk becomes available.
Do not count the 200 sample independently from the related 2010 and 2016 Marikina research until specimen-level overlap is checked.
